correctness.rationale: Uniform symplectic-Lagrangian incidence gives Pr(v nonzero in L)=1/(Q+1), and the step law mu=delta_e/(Q+1)+Q nu/(Q+1), nu uniform on zero-central slice, q odd. For each nontrivial additive central character, the Schrödinger Weyl-slice sum is Q times parity R, so Fourier(mu)=(I+R)/(Q+1), with +1 eigenspace size (Q+1)/2 and -1 size (Q-1)/2. The Q^2 abelian characters give eigenvalues 1 and 1/(Q+1). Counting each dimension-Q irrep Q times gives the stated complete convolution spectrum; finite Fourier inversion yields exactly the point-mass expression. For t>=1 the signed mass excess is on z=0 and deficiency on z!=0 (checked from a_t and b_t); summation gives TV=(q-1)/q*(2/(Q+1))^(t-1). Initial t=0 is expressly excluded from chi-square formula. Independently carried out exact group convolution on every state for q=3,5,m=1 and t=1..4, matching all point masses and TV values; finite tests supplement the Fourier proof for odd prime powers.

originality.rationale: Gross (2006) establishes the standard odd-dimensional Wigner/parity identity used here, and finite Heisenberg Fourier representation is classical. Bump et al. (2015/17) treat sparse few-generator Heisenberg steps. A similarly named November 8 finding averages only TWO fixed complementary coordinate Lagrangian subgroups and has different Fourier spectrum and mixing law t/2^(t-1), not the UNIFORM mixture over all Lagrangians. The complete dense-measure all-time exact total variation and complete PMF do not follow from those prior theorems without a new measure-specific transform and sign calculation. Priority remains bounded.
residual_risks: A general subgroup-averaging Heisenberg walk theorem could implicitly imply the dense all-Lagrangian formula even if not indexed under this measure.
Gross parity operator and representation decomposition are classical, and are not credited as new.
Characteristic two excluded due to the half-symplectic group-coordinate and parity assumption.

value.rationale: Uniform selection from all symplectic Lagrangians is a natural high-symmetry finite Heisenberg walk. An exact full-time point mass and total-variation identity reveals a sharp one-step-to-two-step asymptotic mixing transition, dramatically different from sparse generators and from mixing only two fixed coordinate subgroups; the exact spectrum is reusable for analysis of this walk. This is a motivated structural calculation, not just general Fourier theory restated.

limitations: Odd characteristic, uniform draw over all Lagrangians and no extra central increments only.
Finite checked field orders do not prove all odd prime-power cases.
